messages.text: The backtest ran. To put the result in context, I'll pull SPY's closing prices at the start and end of the window for a buy-and-hold comparison.

I ran the MACD crossover backtest on SPY, because the request didn't name a ticker. SPY was my choice as a broad-market stand-in, not something you asked for. On SPY the strategy lost 0.8% over three years, while simply holding SPY returned about 87.7%.

**Setup:** The strategy buys when the MACD line crosses above its signal line and sells when it crosses back below. It used the standard 12/26/9 settings, ran from 2023-09-27 to 2026-09-25 (the last trading day before today), and started with $10,000.

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total return | -0.79% ($10,000 to about $9,921) |
| Annualized return | -0.38% |
| Sharpe / Sortino | 0.01 / 0.01 |
| Max drawdown | -16.5% |
| Trades | 30 (11 wins, 19 losses, 36.7% win rate) |
| Average win / average loss | +$259 / -$154 (about 1.7 to 1) |
| Profit factor | 0.97 |
| Best trade | +8.5% (+$794), 2026-04-06 to 2026-05-04 |
| Worst trade | -12.5% (-$1,256), 2025-03-24 to 2025-04-07 |
| Average holding period | 9.4 days |

**What drove the result:**
- **Buy-and-hold did far better.** SPY closed at 410.88 on 2023-09-27 and 771.35 on 2026-09-25, a gain of about 87.7% (prices only, no fees). The crossover strategy captured almost none of that.
- **One trade caused most of the drawdown.** The trade opened on 2025-03-24 stayed open through the April 2025 selloff and closed on 2025-04-07 down 12.5%. MACD reacts late, so the sell signal came after most of the drop. That one trade accounts for nearly the whole 16.5% drawdown.
- **The signals flipped often in sideways markets.** From December 2025 to March 2026, entries and exits came within one to six days of each other, and most of those trades lost money.
- **It sat out the start of the window.** The first entry wasn't until 2023-12-21, so it missed the rally from late October to December 2023.
- **The last trade was probably closed by the test itself.** It opened on 2026-09-21 and closed on 2026-09-25, the final day of data, which suggests the test closed it rather than a sell signal.

The tool graded the strategy "F", and its main recommendation was a 1.2% position size under the Kelly formula. That is effectively saying there is no edge.

**Decision for you:** if you meant a specific stock, send the ticker and I'll run the same test on it. I can also search for better MACD settings or test how well a setting holds up over time. I didn't do either, because tuning settings on SPY wouldn't answer your question if you meant a different stock.

Nothing was written or changed: no portfolio, journal or watchlist entries.
